guitar.notes: Eddie Van Halen's homemade 'Frankenstrat' is among the most iconic guitars in rock history, extremely well documented.

tone.summary: A polished 80s clean-crunch tone achieved using a US Deluxe/Silver Twin style amp setup, enhanced by compression and Chorus for the signature Van Halen sheen.
corrections: Use clean-crunch, not Marshall JCM gain
Keep chorus as the key texture

rig.name: Van Halen - Why Can't This Be Love - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and maintain tight rhythm playing.
Provide slight compression and enhance the attack for a polished sheen.
Achieve the clean-crunch edge without heavy distortion or mid-scooping.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is used to simulate a light, biting overdrive/edge-up effect typical of 80s rock, avoiding dedicated high-gain models.

blocks.purpose: Model a bright, articulate clean platform suitable for 80s rock tones.
Provide a bright and focused cabinet sound matching the US Deluxe amp model.
Brighten the overall tone and add clarity to the rhythm parts.
Wah is explicitly avoided per the musical verdict.
Apply the signature chorused sheen required for the 80s Van Halen sound.
Delay is minimized/avoided to keep the tone tight and focused.
blocks.gap: The verdict suggests avoiding heavy delay, so this module is kept available but inactive for rhythm parts.

blocks.purpose: Add subtle space and polish without sounding overly wet or muddy.

improvements.summary: Upgrade IR to enhance 80s polish and brightness.

proposals.reason: Enhance the bright, polished sheen required for 80s Van Halen clean-crunch.
